purpose: Defines the logical data model of doc-link: identity, relationships, versions and primary sources of information such as document info, references, sections and confirmed ToC, without fixing a physical schema.
summary: Model boundary: current actual files and last confirmed index are separate; no notification state is held; key membership does not limit reference validity
Information table: document identity, target specification, observation, document info, reference description, reference check result, section entry, last check state, confirmed ToC, build run
Document info is stored once per doc_link_id and never copied per key, so all keys see the same latest info
Confirmed ToC holds membership, references, reflected hashes, check results, but not document info
Cardinality: a key has many document IDs, a document belongs to many keys, at most one confirmed ToC per key
Reverse references are derived from scanned referrers only, not all referrers in the world
Sections are identified by heading-end section IDs; sections without a DLID have no stable identity
Document ID differs from content hash; link path fixes also change the hash
Reference check match holds only for the recorded directory and time; documents leaving the target are removed from the ToC
tasks: Designing or revising the doc-link data model
Implementing ToC build and confirm logic
Implementing reference check and reverse reference derivation
Reviewing multi-key behavior of document info
